constraints: SI-11 (fixed contract): an unset worker_id is reported as null / omitted key, NEVER a sentinel string ('unknown', '') treated as a present worker. A real worker id is reported verbatim. Downstream spec 00032 inherits the LiveRunRow.worker_id field and asserts it crosses to Postgres parity, so do not change the field name or its null semantics.
Only READ and surface worker_id; this spec changes nothing about how worker_id is WRITTEN (the worker daemon already persists it).

collect_live_rows must continue to read from relational rows only (lifecycles + attempts), include running/validating/awaiting_approval runs sorted by task_id, and add no telemetry-event scan (00011/00025 invariant) -- the full-suite grader guards this.
SI-9: no schema change and no CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION bump; worker_id is an existing v12 column.
Commit the change with a Conventional Commits message (e.g. 'feat:') before reporting done.
Run mcp__ide__getDiagnostics on every .py file you touch and fix all Pylance errors before reporting done.
non_goals: GRADING SURFACE -- do not create, edit, read, or open anything under .flywheel/holdout/00031-spend-and-worker-aggregates/. The held-out worker-id test seeds a specific worker id string your implementation does not see.
Do not weaken, delete, or @skip any existing test under packages/*/tests/.
Do not change the per-task status semantics or the existing status --json keys (task_id, state, latest_run_id, etc.) -- only ADD the in-flight worker_id surfacing.
Do not port collect_live_rows off SqliteStore to the protocol for Postgres parity -- that retype is spec 00032's job; add the field and select it on the current SqliteStore-typed read path.
edge_cases: In-flight run with a non-empty persisted worker_id: the live snapshot entry and the status --json entry both report that exact worker_id string.
In-flight run with an unset (null/empty) worker_id: the snapshot worker_id is None and the JSON key is null or omitted -- never 'unknown' or '' presented as a real worker.
status --json output stays valid JSON (parses with python3 -m json.tool) with the worker_id addition.
A hardcoded worker id must fail the held-out assertion, which compares against the specific seeded id.
